items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: He had a woman named Hattie Burl&son and Victoria Spivay

ctx.x: Yeah, I heard something, about that.

All right. J.Mayo Williams was with the company. And he came down to Dallas. And a man named R. T. Ashford had a record shop and he used to get talent. He had a woman named Hattie Burl&son and Victoria Spivay and those people. And I went to him and I said, "You know, Mr. Ashford, Blind Lemon Jefferson I think will sound good on records." And he said, "Mmmmmh." And he never indicated to me that, you know, that he would negotiate. So he got together with the record company and that's how Blind Lemon Jefferson made…
record. And I didn't get anything for it. Boy, I can certainly reminisce! (Laughter).
